title: Streaming schema gating and gradual JSON-mode adapter
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Our existing JSON-mode enforcement assumes fully-buffered responses and heavy-weight schema validation at the end of generation. This causes two issues for streaming APIs: 1) callers experience long head-of-line latency because we wait to validate the whole payload, and 2) strict post-hoc enforcement often fails in cases where intermediate tokens temporarily violate structural expectations but are corrected later in the stream.

Goal: Build a runtime adapter that validates streaming outputs progressively and applies a configurable gating policy (pass-through, soft-warning, block-and-recover) so we can enforce schema adherence without regressing latency or developer ergonomics. The adapter should integrate with the constrained-decoder shim and be pluggable into Hosted/Dedicated runtimes and the Private control plane.

Design summary:
- Progressive fragment validator: incremental JSON/Scheme-aware parser that checks 'complete fragments' (object/array boundaries, top-level field completeness) as they arrive. It reports three classes of findings: transient-mismatch, deterministic-violation, and completion-violation.
- Gating policy engine: per-route config that maps policy -> action. Example actions: allow-stream (log), warn-and-sample (emit structured warning tokens), block-and-fallback (stop current model, retry with a relaxed schema model), or reject-request. Policies configurable via Console and API.
- Compatibility adapter: For older clients that rely on soft JSON-mode (legacy behavior), support a compatibility mode where the adapter only emits warnings during a 2-week canary and then flips to strict enforcement for selected routes.
- Fallback strategies: automatic re-issue of request to a tolerant decoder, or fall back to non-streaming buffered validation with human-in-the-loop in specific high-risk routes (payments, legal).

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Parser complexity: implementing a streaming JSON validator that tolerates incremental partials requires careful state machine design. We'll reuse the existing constrained-decoder token tagging and maintain a compact stack of open containers; this adds ~1-2MB/runtime of state.
- Latency: validation is O(n) in tokens but runs inline with generation. We'll implement a fast path (lightweight checks for most tokens) and a heavier path triggered on structural boundaries.
- Backwards compatibility: the compatibility adapter must be opt-in per-route to avoid breaking existing customers. Default for new routes is "soft-warning".

Test plan:
- Unit: streaming-parser FSM tests with intentionally interleaved token sequences (including truncated boundaries, early closing braces, escaped characters across buffer boundaries).
- Integration: synthetic stream harness that injects malformed-but-recovering sequences to measure false-positive rates and latency overhead.
- E2E: real-model playback tests using recorded model outputs and regression checks versus the current JSON-mode pipeline.
- Canary: staged rollout to 5% Hosted traffic, then 25%, then 100% after stability gates. Canary monitored by a dashboard tracking schema-violation-rate, latency P95, and customer error reports.

Metrics to monitor:
- schema_violation_rate (per-route), schema_violation_type_breakdown (transient vs deterministic), streaming_latency_p50/p95, request_replay_rate (fallback count), and false_block_rate (customer-facing rejections that are later considered acceptable).

Acceptance criteria:
- Progressive validator reduces buffered validation latency by >=40% on sample streaming routes.
- False_block_rate < 0.1% on canary traffic after tuning.
- No regression in tail latency >5% versus baseline.
- Console exposes policy controls and per-route violation metrics.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge adapter and unit tests behind feature flag.
2) Internal testing with Nightly dataset + synthetic harness.
3) Canary stepwise increase with human in loop on first two hours of rollout.
4) Flip default policy from soft-warning to strict for a small set of internal routes after 2 weeks.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Streaming+Schema+Gating+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123
- Synthetic harness (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/streaming-validator-harness
- Dashboard template: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/streaming-schema-gating

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Over-eager blocking for models that emit non-deterministic tokenization. Mitigation: start in soft-warning, add aggregated sampling of warnings, and provide developers with token-level logs.
- Risk: Increased memory per runtime worker. Mitigation: aggressive object pooling and option to offload heavy checks to a worker thread pool.

Next steps:
- Diego to land the parser FSM and unit tests (ETA 2025-02-28).
- QA to run synthetic harness and report false_positive matrix (ETA 2025-03-07).
- PM to prepare console policy UI mockups and canary checklist (link in comments).
